Your memories, back in\nthe order you took them

Photos moved from your iPhone showing up backwards in Instagram or KakaoTalk? Those apps sort by when a file arrived on the phone, not when it was taken. This app finds each photo\'s real date and re-saves them oldest first.

How it works: each item is copied with identical content, oldest first. Then Android asks you once per batch to allow deleting the originals. If you decline, the copies are removed and nothing changes.

Cloud sync can stay on: re-saved copies are identical to the originals, so Google Photos and the Gallery treat them as the same photos. If some photos still show up twice afterwards, turn off sync in the Gallery (Menu → Settings → Sync photos and videos); your cloud photos are not deleted by that.
Good to know: \"Favorite\" marks in your gallery app may be lost. Your gallery\'s own order does not change. Some apps only show the new order after you restart them.

Help and about
Frequently asked questions
Why are my photos out of order in other apps?

The Gallery sorts by the date a photo was taken, but apps like Instagram sort by when the file arrived on the phone, and apps like KakaoTalk by when the file last changed. Moving thousands of photos at once scrambles those times. This app re-saves your photos in the order they were taken, so all three line up.
How does the app work?

Every photo carries three times: when it was taken, when it arrived on the phone, and when the file last changed. Think of a photo album. The Gallery files each print by the date written on the back, but Instagram shows them in the order they were slipped into the album, and KakaoTalk in the order they were last touched. Moving thousands of photos at once slips them in out of order.

So the app first finds the real date each photo was taken. It reads the camera info inside the photo (EXIF), then the file name, then the file time. Then it re-saves only the out-of-order photos, oldest first, one by one. The order they are re-saved becomes the order they sit in the album, so every app shows them in the order they were taken. It also sets each new file's time to the date it was taken.

Quality stays the same, because the file is copied byte for byte. If you choose to remove the originals, they go to the trash, so you can undo within 30 days.
Will my photos lose quality or change?
No. Each copy is byte-for-byte identical to the original, including photo details such as location.
What happens to the originals?
After copying, Android asks whether the originals may be removed. With \"Keep originals for 30 days\" on, they stay in the trash for 30 days, and you can undo from the first screen until then.
I restored photos from the Gallery trash and now each one shows twice

Android cannot change the order of a photo already on the phone, so this app saves a copy and moves the original to the trash. Restoring the original by hand from the trash brings it back next to the copy. To go back, use \"Undo\" on the first screen instead: it removes the copies first, then restores the originals. If it already happened, delete the restored originals again.
How much free space do I need?
About as much as the photos being fixed, for a short while. The scan screen shows the amount, and the work is split into batches when space is tight.
Will Google Photos or other cloud backups get duplicates?
Re-saved copies are identical to the originals, so they are recognised as the same photos. If you still see some twice, turn the Gallery\'s cloud sync off and on again.
The app says nothing needs fixing, but an app still shows the wrong order
Close that app completely and open it again. If you edited a photo\'s date in the Gallery, its file time may now be today. When the scan offers \"Fix file times\", tap it.
Photos I cropped or edited on the iPhone look unedited
The iPhone keeps the original and the edits separately, and only the original moves to the new phone. This app cannot bring the edits back. You can download the edited photos from icloud.com instead.
Are my photos sent anywhere?
No. The app has no internet permission at all, so it cannot send your photos anywhere. No ads, no account, no data collection.
